plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole avenues turn into tunnels of lavender-purple as the feathery-leaved trees release clouds of trumpet-shaped blooms. When the flowers fall, they carpet streets and pavements in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, peaking in October in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, where tens of thousands of street trees line the city
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, but it thrives so well in Pretoria that it is now considered invasive in parts of South Africa.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped pink-lilac blooms rise from bare ground without any leaves, appearing in damp meadows just as autumn begins. They look like crocuses but are actually members of the lily family.
plants.bloomingSeason: August to November, with October well within the flowering window
plants.location: Meadows and grasslands across southern and central Europe
plants.funFact: The plant is highly toxic and contains colchicine, a compound that is still used in medicine and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.

plants.name: Anigozanthos manglesii
plants.description: Velvety, claw-shaped flowers in vivid red and green sit on tall stems above strappy leaves. They are a spring highlight of the sandy bushland of Western Australia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, with peak colour from August to October
plants.funFact: It is the floral emblem of Western Australia, and its furry flowers are adapted for pollination by nectar-feeding birds.
